title: Scientific Knowledge, Evidence, and Testable Ideas
learning_target: I can explain how scientific ideas are built, tested, and supported by evidence and models.
i_can: I can distinguish observations, inferences, hypotheses, scientific laws, and scientific theories.
evidence_job: Classify scientific knowledge statements by the role they play in evidence building.
likely_misconceptions: observation vs inference; law vs theory hierarchy myth; untestable claims treated as scientific
preferred_question_families: classification; claim-test design; data/model evidence evaluation
representations: short evidence statements, measurements, compact formulas, small data sets
notes_anchor_plan: At least one complete Example/YTI pair; IC3 receives the fourth pair for additional modeling/transfer support.
practice_weighting_rationale: IC1/IC2 receive classification/testability breadth; IC3 receives extra transfer in later practice. Splits: 9/7/8, 7/9/8, 8/7/9, 6/8/10.
secure_assessment_plan: Every form directly samples all three I-cans; IC3 is a constructed evidence/model task.
source_basis: Unit 1 Assessment Plan U1-S1-IC1; Hewitt Ch. 1 observation/measurement evidence structures; existing Bank scenario family retained.

title: Newton's First Law and Inertia
learning_target: I can explain Newton's First Law and use it to predict motion when the net force is zero.
i_can: I can state Newton's First Law in everyday language and apply it to objects at rest or moving.
evidence_job: Use Newton's First Law to predict motion from the net-force condition.
likely_misconceptions: motion requires continuing force; inertia is a force; zero net force means no forces
preferred_question_families: prediction from motion state; misconception diagnosis; interaction identification
representations: motion descriptions, interaction descriptions, low-friction/rest/constant-velocity contexts
notes_anchor_plan: At least one complete Example/YTI pair; IC3 receives the fourth pair for additional modeling/transfer support.
practice_weighting_rationale: IC1/IC2 carry misconception correction early; IC3 varies interaction reasoning across sets. Splits: 8/9/7, 10/7/7, 7/9/8, 9/8/7.
secure_assessment_plan: Every form directly samples all three I-cans with independent conceptual contexts.
source_basis: Unit 1 Assessment Plan U1-S2-IC1; Hewitt 2.3 Newton's First Law tablecloth/space-probe reasoning; existing Bank motion family retained.

title: Forces as Vectors and Net Force
learning_target: I can represent forces as vectors and determine the net force on an object.
i_can: I can explain that a force has both magnitude and direction.
evidence_job: Interpret force as a vector requiring magnitude and direction.
likely_misconceptions: force described by magnitude only; opposite forces added instead of subtracted; arrow direction ignored
preferred_question_families: vector language; collinear calculation; actual arrow-model interpretation
representations: actual inline vector arrows plus quantitative force statements
notes_anchor_plan: At least one complete Example/YTI pair; IC3 receives the fourth pair for additional modeling/transfer support.
practice_weighting_rationale: IC2 receives the largest calculation family because one-dimensional net force needs repeated numerical fluency; IC3 retains recurring actual representations. Splits: 6/10/8, 7/8/9, 5/11/8, 8/7/9.
secure_assessment_plan: Every form includes actual vector-arrow evidence for IC3 plus independent vector/net-force items.
source_basis: Unit 1 Assessment Plan U1-S3-IC1; Hewitt 2.4 vector magnitude-and-direction definition; existing Bank vector-concept family retained.
